questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom.

To bring to light
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. 'To disclose'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"To bring to light"** means to reveal or disclose something that was previously unknown or hidden. (प्रकाश में लाना)

 
 
• **Example: **The investigation brought to light several facts that were previously unknown.
 
 
 
• **"To disclose" **refers to making something known or public; it is the act of revealing information. (प्रकट करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The company disclosed its financial results for the year.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of **'To bring to light' **is **'To disclose'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. 'To disclose'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To engage in conversation **(बातचीत में शामिल होना): To start or participate in a dialogue.

 
 
• **Example:** She loves to engage in conversation with people from different cultures.
 
 
 
• **To lighten **(हल्का करना): To make something less heavy or intense.
 
 
• **Example: **He tried to lighten the mood by telling a joke.
 
 
 
• **To disengage **(अलग करना): To separate or release from something to which it is attached or connected.
 
 
• **Example:** She managed to disengage herself from the conversation without being rude.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(a) false news websites

(b) spreading propaganda about politics

(c) thrive because the advertisements and politicians

(d) and social networking sites

(e) make a lot of money
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 (adcbe).

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Arrange the parts so the sentence has a clear subject, verb and a coherent subordinate clause. 
 
• Start with the subject phrase: (a) false news websites and add the coordinating noun phrase (d) and social networking sites to form the compound subject.
 
• Follow with the main verb phrase (c) thrive because the advertisements and politicians, which introduces the reason clause.
 
• Complete the reason clause with (b) spreading propaganda about politics (modifying “advertisements and politicians”) and end with (e) make a lot of money as the effect inside the clause.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

**Reconstructed sentence: ***False news websites and social networking sites thrive because the advertisements and politicians spreading propaganda about politics make a lot of money.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (aecbd):** This sequence starts awkwardly and does not flow logically.
 
• **Option 3 (****adecb****): **It is not correct because it places "spreading propaganda about politics" before the reason for thriving
 
• **Option 4 (aedcb):** This arrangement makes the sentence difficult to follow, as it misplaces key information about how these websites thrive.

Note: This is a PYP question, and the official answer key has marked (correct option) as the correct answer, hence we cannot make any changes to it.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

P) willing to go

Q) is not

R) my son

S) camping
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (1)** i.e. **RQPS**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence starts with part (R), **"my son,"** which is the subject of the sentence.
 
• Next, part (Q) adds the main verb, saying** "is not,"** which negates the action.
 
• Part (P) continues by introducing the action, **"willing to go,"** indicating the condition of the subject.
 
• Finally, part (S) concludes with the activity,** "camping,"** specifying the activity that my son is not willing to do.

Therefore, the correct answer is RQPS.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (SPRQ):** This option disrupts the natural sequence by placing "willing to go" after the verb.
 
• Option 3 (**PQRS**): This option lacks logical flow and wrong sequence as it misses the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4 (QRSP):** This option begins with a negation that creates an incomplete and awkward structure.

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It was as simple as announcing what you have in your store or the services you offer in your premises.

B. Over the years, advertising has evolved into a major industry that goes beyond informing to persuading and influencing.

C. Advertising was initially meant to make people aware of the goods available in the market.

D. It is a form of brainwashing consumers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph begins by explaining the initial purpose of advertising.
 
• **Sentence C is the first sentence** as it sets the context of the evolution of advertising:
 
 
• "Advertising was initially meant to make people aware of the goods available in the market."
 
 
 
• **Sentence A follows** as it elaborates on the initial simplicity of advertising:
 
 
• "It was as simple as announcing what you have in your store or the services you offer in your premises."
 
 
 
• **Sentence B is the third sentence** because it shows how advertising has evolved over the years:
 
 
• "Over the years, advertising has evolved into a major industry that goes beyond informing to persuading and influencing."
 
 
 
• **Sentence D is the fourth** as it concludes by describing the impact of modern advertising:
 
 
• "It is a form of brainwashing consumers."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **CABD**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Advertising was initially meant to make people aware of the goods available in the market. It was as simple as announcing what you have in your store or the services you offer in your premises. Over the years, advertising has evolved into a major industry that goes beyond informing to persuading and influencing. It is a form of brainwashing consumers."

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

They are building a new hospital in the city.

options.text: A new hospital was built in the city by them.
A new hospital has been built in the city by them.
A new hospital will be built in the city by them.
A new hospital is being built in the city by them.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "They are building a new hospital in the city."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "a new hospital" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "are building" to "is being built" (present continuous passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "them."
 
• Ensure the location phrase "in the city" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A new hospital is being built in the city by them."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"A new hospital was built in the city by them." – Incorrect tense (past simple passive).
 
• **Option 2: **"A new hospital has been built in the city by them." – Incorrect tense (present perfect passive).
 
• **Option 3: **"A new hospital will be built in the city by them." – Incorrect tense (future simple passive).

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined part of the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

As the rulers of the planet, humans like to think that __it is the largest creatures__ that will emerge victorious from the struggle for survival.

options.text: it is the most large creatures

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **they are the largest creatures**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"it is the largest creatures"** is grammatically incorrect and does not agree with the plural subject "humans". (यह सबसे बड़े प्राणी हैं)

 
 
• **Example: **It is the largest creatures that dominate the food chain.
 
 
 
• **"They are the largest creatures" **correctly uses the plural pronoun "they" to refer back to "humans" and maintains subject-verb agreement. (वे सबसे बड़े प्राणी हैं)
 
 
• **Example: **They are the largest creatures that can survive in the harshest environments.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct substitution for the given phrase is **'they are the largest creatures'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **they are the largest creatures**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **No substitution** (कोई प्रतिस्थापन नहीं): This option implies that the original phrase is correct, which it is not in this context.

 
 
• **Example:** As the rulers of the planet, humans like to think that it is the largest creatures that will emerge victorious from the struggle for survival. (Incorrect)
 
 
 
• **It is the most large creatures** (यह सबसे बड़े प्राणी हैं): The phrase "most large" is not grammatically correct; "largest" should be used instead.
 
 
• **Example:** It is the most large creatures that dominate the ecosystem. (Incorrect)
 
 
 
• **They are a largest creature** (वे एक सबसे बड़े प्राणी हैं): This option incorrectly uses "a" with "largest" which is a superlative adjective and should be used with "the".
 
 
• **Example:** They are a largest creature in the ocean. (Incorrect)

questions.question:

They have built a new bridge across the river.

• Change the active verb form "have built" to **"has been built"** (present perfect passive).
 
• Add the preposition** "by"** followed by the original subject "them."
 
• Ensure the phrase **"across the river"** remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

The principal gave up / the prizes to / the winners on / Republic Day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
